title: Short Stuff: The Death of Charles Morgan
summary: Short Stuff episode on the 1977 death of Charles C. Morgan, an escrow agent in Tucson, Arizona, who allegedly helped the mafia launder money through gold and platinum transactions. After a March 1977 abduction and return, he went missing again in May 1977 and was found dead in the desert outside Tucson, shot in the back of the head with his own handgun, wearing a bulletproof vest. The sheriff called it suicide, but his wife Ruth and the hosts consider it murder. The hosts recount the strange clues (a tooth in a handkerchief, a two-dollar bill with Ecclesiastes 12:1-8 notation, an anonymous phone call), and the theory that a hitman lured Morgan with an offer to buy back his contract. Morgan had reportedly been informing on the mafia to the Treasury Department.
topics: money laundering through gold and platinum

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the episode and tease a lesser-known unsolved true crime case.

segments.title: Death of Charles Morgan and the suicide claim
segments.summary: Hosts describe Morgan's death in the desert outside Tucson in May 1977: shot in the back of the head with his own gun, wearing a bulletproof vest, gun without his fingerprints, and the sheriff calling it suicide while his wife disputed it.

segments.title: Morgan's job as escrow agent
segments.summary: Explanation of what an escrow agent does and how the role can be used to launder money; Morgan allegedly laundered mafia money through Arizona using gold and platinum.
topics: money laundering through gold and platinum

segments.title: Laundering mechanics and estimated scale
segments.summary: Hosts explain how illicit money passed through escrow becomes legitimate, and Don Devereaux's estimate of about a billion dollars in transactions.

segments.title: Transition
segments.summary: Brief break and lead-in to the story of Morgan's death.

segments.title: March 1977 disappearance and return
segments.summary: Morgan goes missing for three days in March 1977 and returns zip-tied, missing a shoe, and claiming his throat was painted with a hallucinogen; he tells Ruth not to call police.

segments.title: Life after the abduction
segments.summary: Morgan recovers, wears a bulletproof vest, grows a beard, and drives his daughters to school while refusing to explain to Ruth.

segments.title: Second disappearance and anonymous call
segments.summary: Morgan vanishes again in May 1977 for nine days; Ruth receives an anonymous call from a woman mentioning Ecclesiastes 12:1-8.

segments.title: Clues found with the body
segments.summary: A two-dollar bill clipped inside his underwear bore Ecclesiastes 12 notation, seven Hispanic surnames and a drug smuggling route map; a tooth wrapped in a handkerchief and a note giving burial directions were found in the car.

segments.title: Caller follow-up and motel meeting
segments.summary: A woman who called the sheriff's office identifies herself and says she met Morgan at a motel; he was on the run with a briefcase of money trying to buy back a hit contract.

segments.title: Hitman lure theory and Morgan as informant
segments.summary: Morgan reportedly informed on the mafia to the Treasury Department; Don Devereaux theorizes a hitman lured him into the desert by offering to sell back the contract.

segments.title: Closing remarks
segments.summary: Hosts reflect on the sadness of the case, suggest further reading, and sign off.
